preamble: Assimilation of the coda tap [ɾ] to a following /j/, giving an unreleased voiced palatal stop before the stop realization of /j/: [ɟ˺ɟ]. In western Cuban Spanish (the provinces from Pinar del Río to Matanzas and Cienfuegos, including Havana, plus the municipalities of Corralillo and Trinidad), coda /ɾ/ and coda /l/ merge and assimilate to the next consonant. Inside a word Spanish has no /j/ or /ɲ/ after a coda consonant, so this geminate arises only across word boundaries; Arias (2019) calls [ɟ˺ɟ] and [ɲɲ] "combinaciones exclusivas de la fonética sintáctica". Arias explains the stop as a [ɟ] realization of /j/ whose closure spreads to the preceding liquid. The unassimilated pronunciations remain more common.
phoneticEffects: Regressive Assimilation, Place Assimilation, Fortition, Gemination

languageExamples.context: Word-final, before a word beginning with /j/

examples.note: [ɟ˺] is an unreleased voiced palatal stop.
Arias contrasts das yerbas, pronounced da[h] yerbas, where coda /s/ is aspirated instead.
